Early Years
​Intent
​At George Grenville Academy, we believe that our holistic language based curriculum is the key to success for our children. Exposure to a broad range of inclusive books, environmental walks, engagement with our community and exciting clubs, enable our children to develop a wide range of vocabulary. Communication and language is at the forefront of all we do. Opportunities are maximised through quality interactions, carefully considered learning environments and planned first-hand experiences. Through this approach, our children are enabled to acquire the confidence, knowledge, skills, values, attitudes and behaviours for successful life-long learning.

SEND and Inclusion at George Grenville Academy
InclusionAt George Grenville we promote inclusion through provision that enables all children to reach their potential. We work hard to ensure that all children access a rich and varied curriculum which supports their individual needs. SENDCO & Assistant Head Annie McMillan[email protected]​01280 813273
What should I do if I think my child needs further support?At Grenville, we operate an 'open-door' policy. If you have any concerns regarding the support your child needs, then please speak to your child's class teacher. We hold parent/teacher meetings that last 15-20 minutes at the start of each term but if you cannot wait for that, then please make an appointment by emailing either the school office or your child's teacher. Click on the button below to take you to our contacts page where you can find the appropriate email address or telephone number.
Further Information
Where else can I go for additional support?Annie McMillan (school SENDCo) is available to meet and discuss the support that is needed. She works closely with the teaching staff and outside agencies such as the specialist teacher service, school nursing, education psychology team and county SEND advisors. If your child has an education support plan, this will be reviewed by the teacher and the parents each term and targets reviewed and set. If, for any reason you are not happy with the SEND service from the school, then please come and speak to the Head of School, Sarah Harrison. There is also a school complaints policy on the policy webpage that will detail each stage of the complaints process.

Pattern of the School Day
PE, Drama and Music Lessons
All children from Year 1 to Year 6 will have either music lessons each half term and there will also be drama opportunities planned in throughout the year.
​Please see below for when you child will have PE and will need to come into school dressed in their PE uniform. Children are to come to school dressed in their PE uniforms on the days they have PE. This is to avoid having to change clothes close to each other in classes. It will also maximise the time they can spend on their physical education and mean that you are able to wash their PE kits at home. Equality Objectives
​By 2026, we will ensure our school ethos and culture celebrates diversity and promotes tolerance and an understanding and awareness of different families, religious beliefs, backgrounds and cultures within our school community and the wider world.
​By 2026, the gap in attainment and achievement between pupils identified as disadvantaged pupils and non-disadvantaged pupils will have closed across the curriculum
​By 2026 the attendance gap between pupils who have been identified as disadvantaged, including pupils with SEND and those who are not will have closed
